CausalChain: DDR gene alterations → Accumulation of DNA damage and increased neoantigen load → Elevated tumor mutational burden → Potential for immune recognition, but simultaneously → Upregulation of TGF‐β signaling in the TME → Suppression of immune effector cells → Combined PARP inhibition (targeting DDR defects) + Dual PD‑L1/TGF‑β blockade → Reversal of immunosuppression and enhanced antitumor immunity
Hypothesis: BTCs with coexistent DDR deficiencies and a TGF‑β–enriched immunosuppressive microenvironment will respond synergistically to a combination therapy of PARP inhibitors and dual PD‑L1/TGF‑β blockade, resulting in improved antitumor efficacy compared to either strategy alone.
Abstract: We propose a novel hypothesis that a subset of biliary tract cancers (BTCs) defined by concurrent DNA damage repair (DDR) deficiencies and an immunosuppressive, TGF‐β–rich tumor microenvironment (TME) exhibit a high neoantigen load and enhanced tumor mutational burden. Although DDR defects increase the availability of neoantigens that can potentially activate antitumor immune responses, the simultaneous presence of elevated TGF‐β activity impairs immune cell infiltration and effector functions. Therefore, we hypothesize that the integration of a PARP inhibitor (to exploit DDR deficiencies) with a dual blockade targeting both PD‑L1 and TGF‐β will synergistically reprogram the TME, boost immunogenicity, and improve therapeutic responses in this otherwise resistant BTC population.
